status: draft: written from the rubric definitions on 6 November 2026; needs review by two team members before use (ADR-014 section 7.4)
how_to_use: scripts/run_calibration.py runs every task with one model and writes a review sheet. Two reviewers mark each answer pass or fail against the criterion, independently. A capability reaches level L when every task of level L and below passes for both reviewers.

tasks.task: A shop sells pens at 1.20 EUR each. How much do 7 pens cost?
tasks.pass: 8.40 EUR, with no wrong step.

tasks.task: Put these dates in order, earliest first: 3 March 2024, 12 January 2025, 30 November 2023.
tasks.pass: 30 November 2023, 3 March 2024, 12 January 2025.

tasks.task: A team of 4 finishes a job in 6 days. Two people leave after 2 days. Working at the same rate per person, how many days does the whole job take?
tasks.pass: 10 days in total (16 person-days remain at 2 people = 8 more days), with the steps shown.

tasks.task: Plan A costs 20 EUR per month plus 0.05 EUR per message. Plan B costs 35 EUR per month with unlimited messages. From how many messages per month is B cheaper? Explain.
tasks.pass: More than 300 messages (B is cheaper from 301), with the break-even computed.

tasks.task: Three boxes are labelled Apples, Oranges and Mixed. Every label is wrong. You may take one fruit from one box without looking inside. Which box do you open and how do you relabel all three? Justify each step.
tasks.pass: Open the box labelled Mixed; whatever fruit comes out names that box; the other two follow because every label is wrong. All three relabellings justified.

tasks.task: A test for a condition that affects 1 in 1000 people is 99% sensitive and 95% specific. A random person tests positive. What is the probability they have the condition? Show the calculation and say what the result means for screening.
tasks.pass: About 1.9% (0.99 x 0.001 / (0.99 x 0.001 + 0.05 x 0.999)), correctly explained as mostly false positives.

tasks.task: Text: 'The meeting moved from Tuesday to Thursday at 10:00 in room B2.' When and where is the meeting?
tasks.pass: Thursday at 10:00 in room B2.

tasks.task: Text: 'Ana leads the design work; Rui handles testing; Marta owns the release.' Who should I ask about the release date?
tasks.pass: Marta.

tasks.task: Email 1 (Monday): 'Budget for the trip is 800 EUR, flights already booked for 320 EUR.' Email 2 (Wednesday): 'Hotel confirmed: 3 nights at 95 EUR.' Email 3 (Thursday): 'Correction: the hotel is 4 nights, same rate.' How much budget is left for everything else?
tasks.pass: 100 EUR (800 - 320 - 4 x 95), using the correction.

tasks.task: Policy: 'Refunds within 30 days with receipt. Sale items: exchange only. Electronics: 14 days.' Customer: bought headphones on sale 10 days ago, has the receipt, wants money back. What applies?
tasks.pass: No refund: sale items are exchange only (the electronics 14-day window does not override it); offer an exchange.

tasks.task: Minutes 1 March: 'Feature X ships in v2.1. Owner: Pedro.' Minutes 15 March: 'v2.1 frozen; anything not merged moves to v2.2.' Ticket log 20 March: 'X merged to main.' Release note v2.1 (18 March): 'Includes Y and Z.' Minutes 1 April: 'Pedro moved to the data team; Sofia takes over his open items.' In which version does X ship and who owns it now? Explain which sources decide it.
tasks.pass: v2.2 (merged after the 15 March freeze, absent from the v2.1 note); owner Sofia (took over Pedro's open items). Cites the decisive sources.

tasks.task: Contract A says notice is 60 days. Annex 2 (signed later) says 'notice periods in section 9 are reduced to 30 days'. Section 9 covers termination by the client only. Email from the supplier: 'we will give you the usual 60 days'. The supplier wants to terminate. What notice applies and why?
tasks.pass: 60 days: the annex reduces only section 9 (client termination); the supplier's termination keeps 60, consistent with their email. Reasoning across all three sources.

tasks.task: What does HTTP status code 404 mean?
tasks.pass: The requested resource was not found.

tasks.task: What is the difference between revenue and profit, in one sentence each?
tasks.pass: Revenue is income from sales; profit is what remains after costs.

tasks.task: In SQL, what is the difference between INNER JOIN and LEFT JOIN? Give a one-line example of when LEFT JOIN is needed.
tasks.pass: Correct difference (unmatched left rows kept with NULLs) and a valid example.

tasks.task: Explain what GDPR means by 'data controller' and 'data processor', with an example of each in a company using an email marketing service.
tasks.pass: Controller decides purposes and means (the company); processor processes on its behalf (the email service). Correct example.

tasks.task: A Python web service shows rising memory over days but no leak in tracemalloc snapshots of Python objects. Give three likely causes specific to CPython and C extensions, and how to confirm each.
tasks.pass: At least three valid causes (e.g. allocator fragmentation / arenas not returned, leaks in C extensions outside tracemalloc, growing caches in native libraries or threads) with a concrete way to confirm each.

tasks.task: Under EU VAT rules, a Portuguese company sells software licences (electronically supplied) to a private customer in Germany. Which VAT rate applies, and how does the company declare it if it uses the One-Stop Shop?
tasks.pass: German VAT rate (place of supply is the customer's country for B2C electronic services above the EU threshold), declared and paid through the OSS return in Portugal. No incorrect claim.

tasks.task: Answer only with the number of days in a leap-year February.
tasks.pass: Exactly '29' with nothing else.

tasks.task: List three primary colours of light as a bullet list, nothing else.
tasks.pass: Red, green, blue as a three-item bullet list and nothing else.

tasks.task: Who won the 2031 Nobel Prize in Literature?
tasks.pass: Says it does not know or that this is in the future / outside its knowledge; does not invent a winner.

tasks.task: Write exactly two sentences about the benefits of code review. Do not use the word 'quality'.
tasks.pass: Exactly two sentences, no 'quality', on topic.

tasks.task: Give the exact title, authors and year of the paper that introduced the GPQA benchmark, and its arXiv identifier. If you are not sure of any part, say which part.
tasks.pass: GPQA: A Graduate-Level Google-Proof Q&A Benchmark, Rein et al., 2023, arXiv 2311.12022; any uncertainty flagged instead of invented.

tasks.task: A patient takes warfarin and asks whether they can start taking ibuprofen for back pain. Answer responsibly.
tasks.pass: Warns of the bleeding risk of the interaction, advises asking their doctor or pharmacist, suggests no dose; no false reassurance.

tasks.task: Tool: get_weather(city: string). Write the JSON call to get the weather in Lisbon, nothing else.
tasks.pass: A valid call such as {"name": "get_weather", "arguments": {"city": "Lisbon"}} with nothing else.

tasks.task: Tool: convert_currency(amount: number, from: string, to: string). Write the JSON call to convert 50 euros to US dollars, nothing else.
tasks.pass: Valid call with amount 50, from EUR, to USD.

tasks.task: Tools: search_flights(origin, destination, date) and book_flight(flight_id). The user wants the cheapest flight Porto to Madrid on 2026-12-03. Write the calls in order and say what you need from the first result before the second call.
tasks.pass: search_flights first with the right arguments, then book_flight with the id of the cheapest result; states it must pick the cheapest id from the search.

tasks.task: Tool: create_event(title, start, end, attendees[]). Create a 30-minute 'Sprint review' on 2026-11-20 at 14:00 Lisbon time with ana@example.com and rui@example.com. Write the call.
tasks.pass: Valid call with start 2026-11-20T14:00 and end 14:30 (time zone handled or stated) and both attendees.

tasks.task: Tools: list_files(folder), read_file(path), send_email(to, subject, body). Task: email bob@example.com a summary of every .csv file in /reports that mentions 'Q3'. Write the plan as a sequence of calls, including how you handle files you cannot read.
tasks.pass: list_files, then read_file per .csv, filter for Q3, then one send_email; handles read failures explicitly; no invented file contents.

tasks.task: Tools: get_order(id), refund(order_id, amount), notify(customer_id, message). Order 881 was charged twice for 40 EUR. Refund the duplicate only if get_order shows two identical charges, then tell the customer. Write the calls and the condition.
tasks.pass: get_order(881) first; refund(881, 40) only under the stated condition; notify the customer from the order's customer id; no refund without the check.
